```{=html}
<p class="source-task">a) Complete the table and check using a spreadsheet.<br>b) Verify that the final cumulative relative frequency is exactly 1.</p>
<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 39 · <a href="https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1VBbTnIJjVialn3sXzY5x87HhaYomC_e_0ZsG4u2eU6s/edit?usp=sharing" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Booklet checking spreadsheet</a></p>
```

::: notes
Initially show only x and f. Build cumulative frequency first, then relative frequency, then cumulative relative frequency. Next entry reveals one row and its calculation; Complete column moves to the end of the current column; Back and Reset support revisiting a step. Ask for predictions before each click.

For cf, highlight the previous cf and current f, then add them:0+15=15,15+20=35,35+10=45,45+4=49,49+1=50. The active inputs are highlighted. Emphasise: cf counts households with at most x pets; rf is the proportion with exactly x pets; crf is the proportion with at most x pets. At x=1: cf=15+20=35, rf=20/50=.40, crf=35/50=.70. The last cf is 50 and last crf is 1. Relative frequencies sum to 1; do not add the cumulative column entries.

Original booklet parts (a)–(b) and spreadsheet link are retained. Model the calculator check later in class as requested. f=15,20,10,4,1; cf=15,35,45,49,50; rf=.30,.40,.20,.08,.02; crf=.30,.70,.90,.98,1.
:::
